bull.b: Life Time's subscription-like membership base and demonstrated pricing power (ARPM +11.8%, dues +12.3%) create durable, predictable revenue. Higher per-member revenue reduces reliance on membership unit growth and supports margin sustainability from in-club ancillary services and increased utilization.

Margins have meaningfully improved—adjusted EBITDA margin rising and TTM operating margin near 19%—reflecting scalable in-center businesses and cost discipline. Sustained higher margins bolster ROE, fund reinvestment, and make earnings less dependent on high revenue growth.

bull.t: Solid operating cash generation & capital discipline
bull.b: Operating cash flow is solid and improving, and management uses sale‑leasebacks and targeted buybacks to manage liquidity and capital allocation. Reliable operating cash plus explicit FCF targets support debt service and provide a durable framework for disciplined expansion.

bear.b: Despite improvement, leverage remains materially elevated for a leisure business. High debt levels increase refinancing and interest-rate risk, reduce financial flexibility for downturns, and constrain the pace of rollouts or opportunistic spending absent continued strong cash generation.

bear.t: Negative free cash flow amid heavy capex
bear.b: Life Time generates strong operating cash but free cash flow is negative due to elevated capex for club openings. Structural investment needs to grow the footprint mean cash conversion remains strained, complicating deleveraging and increasing reliance on financing or asset monetizations.

Smaller-format MIORA and adjacent services remain immature and delayed, limiting near-term diversification. Execution and regulatory uncertainty for adjunct offerings (e.g., peptide treatments) can postpone expected revenue and margin contributions and increase continuing investment without immediate payoff.
